BiblicalUsage: Self-control — temperance. It stands in the ladder of graces in 2 Peter 1:6, beside knowledge and patience and godliness, and Paul reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come until Felix trembled in Acts 24:25. It is also a fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:23, against which there is no law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe self-control is not willpower but fruit — the Spirit grows it in me the way He grows love and peace. I hold that the man who cannot govern himself is not free, and the Spirit's temperance is the freedom I actually want.
RelatedTopics: Fruit of the Spirit; Godliness; Temptation
